visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young woman with long dark hair, wearing a light pink ruffled off-the-shoulder top and a red bow in her hair, sits on a beige couch wearing black over-ear headphones. She speaks into a professional black Shure microphone attached to a boom arm, smiling brightly with visible facial expressions and moving her lips. The background features neutral-colored curtains and a bright window providing natural illumination. (2) The camera cuts to a man sitting on the same beige couch, wearing a black knit sweater, a black baseball cap, and clear-framed glasses with large headphones. He gesticulates broadly with his right hand, pointing and waving to emphasize his speech while leaning slightly forward towards his microphone. The studio setting is clean, with the couch and microphones being the central objects in the middle-ground. (3) Frequent straight cuts alternate between the woman listening attentively with small nods and the man explaining a concept with active hand gestures. Various white and black Chinese text overlays appear intermittently across the bottom third of the frame. At one point, a specific graphic showing '51:49' appears next to the man's head, accompanied by white radiating impact lines for visual emphasis. (4) The woman is shown speaking again, gesturing with her hands while looking towards the man off-camera. She appears engaged, with her eyes widening and mouth moving as she reacts to the conversation. The lighting remains bright and consistent throughout, highlighting the textures of their clothing and the sleek metallic surfaces of the microphones. (5) The final sequence shows a full-screen graphic overlay featuring large white Chinese characters, promotional text, and a date/time. In the background, blurred footage of the man continues to play as he finishes his point, maintaining the visual continuity of the podcast environment.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to educate viewers on the 'Spiral of Silence' (沈默螺旋效應) psychological concept. It uses a conversational podcast format to break down how minority opinions are often suppressed by a perceived majority, using contemporary political figures like Ko Wen-je as an illustrative example to increase relatability for a social media audience.
